findings.title: Cleanup registered for literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP alias
findings.body: Inside the creation loop the cleanup is `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove`, which uses the string literal "alias" rather than the loop's `alias`. The cleanup therefore targets a nonexistent IDP and the 21 IDPs created by this test (`idp-alias-0` to `idp-alias-20`) are never removed. They can leak into other tests and change counts that depend on the realm's IDPs. The same defect appears at line 425 for `idp-alias-20`, and it was copied from the existing `testCacheIDPByOrg`. The cleanup should reference the actual alias.

findings.title: Invalidation on create/remove of a login-eligible IDP is not tested
findings.body: The test only checks that adding or removing an IDP that is NOT available for login leaves the login caches intact. No scenario creates or removes an IDP that IS login-eligible and asserts that the caches are invalidated. That is the main path covered by the new `registerIDPLoginInvalidation` calls in `create()` and `remove()`. A regression there, such as a wrong `null` or predicate handling in `remove`, would go undetected. The test also never exercises a disabled organization with a cached IDP, nor the wrapped `isEnabled` re-check in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean`.

findings.title: remove() now always hits the database for the IDP before removal
findings.body: `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` is now called unconditionally, whereas it was previously only called when the alias key was already invalidated. When the IDP is cached, a database lookup is added to every remove just to evaluate the login predicate. Using the cached model, or loading it via `getByAlias` through the cache, would avoid the extra query. In addition, a null result is only handled for the new login invalidation; the `isInvalid` branch still passes a possibly null `storedIdp` into `registerIDPInvalidation`.
